name: Interlochen Center for the Arts
watch: Epstein attended Interlochen's summer camp in 1967 and gave money to it from 1990 to 2003, including a $200,000 gift, acknowledged in February 1994, for a lodge on Green Lake named after him. A witness at Ghislaine Maxwell's 2021 trial and a second woman say Epstein and Maxwell met them at the camp at 13 and 14, from 1994, and DOJ files show the pair met a student alone at the lodge.
why_flagged: Private nonprofit arts academy and camp. Gifts were $24.1M in fiscal 2025. Its 2025 report names trustee David Wu, the Foster Family Foundation, DeRoy Testamentary Foundation and Walker Foundation.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2020 to 2026 and audited statements for 2020 to 2024, with named funds in the 2025 report and 31 trustees.

name: Israel Museum
funding: American Friends of the Israel Museum raised over $450M since 1972. Mandel and Safra foundations each gave $12M in 2009. The 2025 report filed with the Israeli register puts state and city grants at 21 percent of income and donations at 27 percent, mostly from abroad, with 39 percent from sources the register does not describe.
watch: In July 2009 PACBI, the Palestinian BDS campaign, urged Yinka Shonibare in an open letter not to guest-curate here. He held a 2010 show.
why_flagged: American Friends of the Israel Museum raised over $450M since 1972. Mandel and Safra foundations each gave $12M in 2009. The 2025 report filed with the Israeli register puts state and city grants at 21 percent of income and donations at 27 percent, mostly from abroad, with 39 percent from sources the register does not describe.
records_note: Its website would not load; a search shows a named board page, and the Israeli register lists it as a public benefit company.

name: Istanbul Biennial (İKSV)
funding: Run by İKSV. Koç Holding is main sponsor for 2007 to 2036. Its group includes oil refiner Tüpraş, almost half its revenue, and defence maker Otokar.
watch: Direnal-Istanbul protested Koç's sponsorship at the 2009 opening. In 2013 protesters wore Koç banners. The 2025 edition drew over 600,000 visitors.
why_flagged: Run by İKSV. Koç Holding is main sponsor for 2007 to 2036. Its group includes oil refiner Tüpraş, almost half its revenue, and defence maker Otokar.
records_note: Reports run from 2013 to 2025, the 2024 one with income and expense tables; Biennial sponsors are named and the trustees and directors are listed.

name: Istanbul Modern
funding: Founding sponsor Eczacıbaşı; main sponsor Doğuş Group with Bilgili Holding. The September 2026 sponsor panel lists Volvo, Visa, Mercedes-Benz, Nescafe, Paribu, TAV Airports and the Istanbul municipality.
watch: A December 2023 sit-in delivered over 5,500 signatures for full-day free entry and open data. Eight artists and a collective pulled works in 2011.
why_flagged: Founding sponsor Eczacıbaşı; main sponsor Doğuş Group with Bilgili Holding. The September 2026 sponsor panel lists Volvo, Visa, Mercedes-Benz, Nescafe, Paribu, TAV Airports and the Istanbul municipality.
records_note: It posts no annual reports or accounts; its sponsor page is one logo panel dated September 2026, and its administration page names the board.

name: IVAM Institut Valencià d'Art Modern
funding: Run by the Generalitat Valenciana's culture department; no operating budget found. 202,258 visitors in 2025. It bought 16 works by 14 women artists for about EUR 1M.
watch: Director Enguita resigned in February 2024 after the Vox-led culture department, which funds IVAM, reported her land donation to prosecutors. They archived it in March.
why_flagged: Run by the Generalitat Valenciana's culture department; no operating budget found. 202,258 visitors in 2025. It bought 16 works by 14 women artists for about EUR 1M.
records_note: No annual report; accounts for 2012 to 2025 with audit reports are posted, the Consejo Rector is listed, and sponsors appear only as two logos.

name: Iziko South African National Gallery
watch: In December 2025 management covered 11 works in Steven Cohen's retrospective the night before opening. SWEAT and Sisonke protested Mthethwa's work in December 2016.
why_flagged: National public entity, an agency of the Department of Arts and Culture (now Sport, Arts and Culture). No corporate sponsor is named on its site.
records_note: Posts annual reports from 2003/04 to 2025/26 with audited statements and donor sections, and names its nine-member council; the site itself lists no donors.

name: Jehangir Art Gallery
watch: In April 2013 the gallery and Mumbai police made Eleena Banik remove two goddess paintings. In 2006 it had a student cover a nude sculpture.
why_flagged: Built 1952 on Sir Cowasji Jehangir's gift in memory of his son. A committee chaired by Adi H. Jehangir manages it; no sponsors or ongoing funders are listed.
records_note: The gallery names its management committee with chairman Adi Jehangir, but publishes no reports, accounts or sponsors.

name: Jewish Museum and Tolerance Center
watch: Endowment managed via Gazprombank asset management per Kommersant; the museum's partners page is empty. Vekselberg also sits on the Tretyakov board.
why_flagged: Partners page lists VTB Bank, Sberbank, SAFMAR foundation, Severstal and Metalloinvest, with Rosneft as an exhibition partner. Founding donors in 2012 to 2014 included Vekselberg, Abramovich and Blavatnik.
records_note: The museum shows partner logos with no date and posts no annual report, accounts or board list; a news item mentions a board meeting.

name: Johannesburg Art Gallery
watch: Joburg Heritage Foundation and Friends of JAG sent the City a legal demand in August 2024 and weighed an interdict in January 2025.
why_flagged: Owned and run by the City of Johannesburg; no corporate sponsor is named. Joburg Heritage Foundation and Friends of JAG back a funded rescue plan.
records_note: Publishes no annual reports, accounts, funders or board of its own; the City of Johannesburg runs the gallery and the Heritage Foundation posts rescue updates.

name: John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts
funding: Congress pays for the federally owned building; programmes run on ticket sales and private gifts. Trump became chair in February 2025; a $100M FY2026 revenue shortfall was projected.
watch: Trump fired the president and board in February 2025. Hamilton, Issa Rae, Renée Fleming and Philip Glass pulled out of the Center.
why_flagged: Congress pays for the federally owned building; programmes run on ticket sales and private gifts. Trump became chair in February 2025; a $100M FY2026 revenue shortfall was projected.
records_note: Its annual reports run 2017 to 2023 with financial reports for 2021 to 2023; Form 990s are on ProPublica; funders and board were not checked.

name: Jordan National Gallery of Fine Arts
funding: Patrons by tier, logos dated May 2024 to Aug 2025: Diamond UAE Ministry of Culture and Youth, Hikma, Jordan Bromine; Platinum Barjeel, Arab Potash; Gold Shoman Foundation; Silver Jordan Phosphate Mines, Jordan Petroleum Refinery, Jordan Kuwait Bank; Bronze four banks, Kemapco.
watch: Flags rest on the UAE ministry, a Gulf state body at Diamond tier, and the state-owned Jordan Petroleum Refinery. The Shoman Foundation is Arab Bank's; its 2014 US terror-financing verdict, settled 2015 and overturned 2018, is a B-level controversy outside the flags.
why_flagged: Patrons by tier, logos dated May 2024 to Aug 2025: Diamond UAE Ministry of Culture and Youth, Hikma, Jordan Bromine; Platinum Barjeel, Arab Potash; Gold Shoman Foundation; Silver Jordan Phosphate Mines, Jordan Petroleum Refinery, Jordan Kuwait Bank; Bronze four banks, Kemapco.
records_note: The gallery names patrons by tier on a partners page, undated, and its trustees on the about page; it publishes no reports or accounts.

name: Joslyn Art Museum
funding: $11.3M expenses (2023); Joslyn endowment (newspaper-syndicate fortune) and private donors.
watch: 2024 pavilion named for Tenaska (natural gas) founder Howard Hawks; uses Bloomberg Connects. No donor roster published; no protest found.
